title: The Authorization *Gap*
dek: Anthropic's $81B IPO is the accountability event AI needed. This week's other stories document everything the IPO doesn't cover.

stories.label: raised in the largest IPO in history, 17% first-day gain
stories.headline: The IPO relocates the safety debate from philosophy to quarterly earnings.

stories.label: of Claude Opus 5.5's cost, per Microsoft's own benchmarks
stories.headline: On IPO day, Microsoft claims 96% of Anthropic's best at one-twentieth the price.

stories.label: of AMD GPU capacity in a six-year deal with TensorWave
stories.headline: AMD is now a production choice for OpenAI, not a Nvidia hedge.
Citi, PNC, and Citizens say agent damage is your problem. Arizona AG says it's OpenAI's.

stories.label: chatbots produced viable terror attack plans in spring 2026 testing
stories.headline: The plans were viable. The guardrails didn't stop misrepresentation.

stories.label: engineers at one startup all denied US visas for CES
stories.headline: The hardware competition is now being managed through immigration policy.

still_signal: Anthropic's IPO creates financial accountability. Who answers when agents act in accounts or chatbots plan attacks is still being written in bank fine print and criminal complaints.
